To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the low‐dose “halo” parts of proton beamlets have a significant influence on the central axis dose of square fields formed with scanned proton beamlets.
small changes in low‐dose regions far from the central axes of proton beamlets produce significant changes in central axis doses of scanned beam proton therapy beams.
the accuracy of proton dose prediction algorithms is highly dependent on the modeling of the low‐dose part of the lateral profiles of individual beamlets.

the dependence of central‐axis doses and output factors for square fields formed by scanned beamlets on the low dose parts (halo) of the lateral dose distributions of the individual beamlets.
the development of a novel and efficient dose calculation algorithm for scanned proton beams, which will be based on our results and the findings of this study.
the accuracy of modeling of proton beamlets for the purpose of dose prediction for scanned proton beam therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dependence of central dose and output factor of square fields on the lateral profile of the beamlet is significant, and the low dose halo of the beamlet should be taken into account for accurate dose prediction algorithms.
the accuracy of the dose calculation algorithms for proton beams is dependent on the accuracy of the modeling of the low dose tails in the beamlet lateral profiles.
the dependence of central dose and output factors on the halo dose is highly significant and should be considered in future dose computation algorithms for proton therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy of proton dose calculations depends on the accuracy of modeling the halo doses.

we have developed a novel approach for modeling the dose from scanned proton beam, and we are currently using this approach to develop a new dose calculation algorithm for scanned proton beam therapy.

the dose output factors for scanned proton beam are very sensitive to lateral profiles of beamlets, and that the low dose halo of beamlet profiles must be modeled with great accuracy to achieve the desired accuracy in dose predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dose prediction accuracy of contemporary algorithms for scanned charged particle beam dose prediction is highly dependent on the modeling of the halo of the individual beamlets, which is far outside the beam axis.
the accuracy of the dose calculation algorithms for scanned proton beams is highly dependent on the correct modeling of the dose far away from the beam axis (i.e. the “halo”).
the accuracy of the dose predictions for scanned proton therapy is highly dependent of the correct modeling of the low‐dose “halo” around individual proton beamlets.
